summary:
### Key Topics Discussed
- Error identification.
- The core problem of the order concept, focusing on its purpose to create tasks that are fundamentally articles with attached data.
- Distinguishing between subscriptions, call-offs, and schedules.
- Post-billing (after the job is done) versus subscriptions (recurring based on an agreement).
- Task creation based on an order concept, including desired delivery times.
- How tasks appear in rough planning with different desired delivery times.
- Future concept of subscriptions defined over a specific period (e.g., one or more years) and recurring with certain periodicity.
- Automatic creation of tasks (uppehållspiffar) by Replit or Trivo based on metadata for multiple rounds over time.
- Side function in Replit or Trivo to summarize order volume for monthly or quarterly invoicing.
- Invoicing for subscriptions based on annual volume divided by billing frequency (e.g., quarterly or monthly).
- Requirement for a new invoice template in Replit that specifies the period and objects covered by the wash in accordance with the agreement.
- Handling of subscription invoices by Replit and their transfer to Fortnox for invoicing.
- Accounting implications for invoices, specifically coding against a separate article for correct accounting entries (customer receivables).
- The complexity of handling subscription invoices with special accounting in Replit/Trivo that needs to identify already invoiced tasks to ensure correct billing.
- Creation of a reconciliation invoice (avräkningsfaktura) from Trivo to Fortnox for completed tasks that are already covered by pre-paid subscriptions.
- Handling of additional services not covered by a subscription, such as extra containers or room cleaning, which should be billed separately.
- The concept of a single invoice issued to the customer that combines pre-paid services (zero cost) and additional, separately billed services.

### Decisions Made
- The current focus has been on post-billing where the invoice is created after the work is performed.
- The complex issue of subscription invoicing, particularly how invoices from Replit/Trivo will account for tasks already covered by subscription payments, will be postponed to a later stage.
- Replit should focus on generating invoices that distinguish between pre-paid subscription services (billed at zero cost) and additional services (billed separately) on the same invoice.
- A separate case will be created to clarify how invoices are generated for scheduled services.

### Action Items
- Replit needs to develop a new invoice template that includes specific text detailing the scope of services (e.g., "washes on these objects during this period in accordance with the agreement").
- Replit needs to ensure subscription invoices are coded against a separate article for correct accounting in Fortnox.

### Important Points & Insights
- The primary function of the order concept is to generate tasks that include an article with appended data, specifying "where" and "when". The type of task is a secondary detail.
- Replit observes a difference between subscriptions, call-offs, and schedules.
- Subscriptions typically involve multiple runs based on the agreement.
- A standard call-off order concept points to a specific run, for example, a wash in June 2026 for specific objects with certain details.
- If a wash is for September 2026, the planner or order receiver copies the initial concept and changes the desired delivery time from June to September, creating new associated tasks.
- These tasks will appear identical in rough planning, except for their desired delivery time, and are then grouped together.
- For future subscriptions, Replit or Trivo should automatically create tasks based on metadata of specified objects, resulting in multiple rounds of tasks for the same object over the subscription period.
- There should be a function to summarize the order volume for monthly or quarterly invoicing based on the established order mass.
- Invoicing for subscriptions should be based on the total annual volume, divided by the billing frequency (e.g., four for quarterly, twelve for monthly).
- Replit will create subscription invoices which will then be sent to Fortnox for actual invoicing.
- Each invoice issued will be accounted for as a customer receivable in accordance with Swedish accounting law.
- When a pre-paid subscription task is performed, a reconciliation invoice from Trivo needs to be sent to Fortnox, detailing the completed service and associated accounting entries to balance against the pre-paid amount.
- The system must recognize when the number of serviced items exceeds the subscription agreement (e.g., 11 containers washed when 10 were pre-paid), prompting additional billing.
- Additional services, like cleaning a room not part of the subscription, should be added to the customer's invoice as a separate line item, potentially originating from a separate order but appearing on the same final invoice.

### Open Questions/Pending Items
- The exact implementation details for Replit's new invoice template and the complexity of its integration.
- Specifics on how the separate article for subscription invoice coding will be defined and managed within Replit/Fortnox.
- How Replit or Trivo will handle special accounting for subscription invoices to correctly identify which tasks have already been charged under a subscription agreement and ensure accurate billing for any additional charges.
- Details on the accounting entries (kontering) for the reconciliation invoices that balance out pre-paid subscription amounts against completed work.
- How invoices for scheduled services will be created and handled.
